components: a looped right body with a descending tail
strokeOrder: curl around the inner-left loop and descend to the lower-left join — then lift once
set the pen at the left side, climb around the rounded outer body, and descend to the lower join — then lift a second time
draw the lower joining bar from the left body to the right — then lift a third time
loop around the right body and finish with its descending tail
strokeOrderNote: four strokes — the inner-left curl, rounded outer-left body, lower joining bar, and looped right body with descending tail are separate pen-down runs; source-verified against the four numbered strokes in Learn Tamil Through English/Hindi

strokeOrderSource.citation: Ratnakar Narale, Learn Tamil Through English/Hindi, Reading and Writing Tamil Granthakshars, Third Tamil Granthakshar ஷ, Sanskrit Hindi Research Institute, p. 13
strokeOrderSource.variation: The printed ஷ diagram numbers four separate pen-down runs in order. This four-run learner path fits those runs to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline; Tamil handwriting varies by school.

notes: Grantha-derived ṣa appears in borrowed words such as சந்தோஷம் (cantōṣam, happiness). Its four-run construction distinguishes the curled left body from the loop-and-tail at the right.
